jobs.jd_text:
**About SiPhox Health**

SiPhox Health is building the leading home testing platform for biomarkers across inflammation, hormones, and metabolic and cardiovascular health. Six in ten Americans live with a chronic disease, and our mission is to make early detection possible from home.

We operate two business lines, both scaling quickly:

1\. Mail-in blood testing: Growing more than 50% quarter over quarter, and the most comprehensive and highly rated at-home blood testing available today.

2\. At-home blood testing device: Planned launch in 2027. Our chip-based module combines biochemistry with integrated photonics, electronics, and microfluidics, protected by more than 50 patents.

SiPhox is an MIT startup backed by Tier I investors including Y Combinator, Khosla Ventures, and Intel Capital.

**The Role**

As Head of Consumer Experience, you will own the end-to-end D2C customer experience and help build the systems, insights, and product experiences that drive long-term consumer engagement and retention.

This role sits at the intersection of Customer Experience, Product, Growth, Retention, and Relationship Management. You will be responsible for deeply understanding our consumers, identifying friction throughout the customer journey, and working cross-functionally to create experiences that make customers successful, engaged, and loyal to SiPhox.

You will serve as the internal voice of the consumer and partner closely with Engineering & Engineering, Sales & Marketing, and G&A to ensure that customer feedback directly informs product development and business strategy.

The ideal candidate is highly customer-centric but also deeply analytical. You understand that strong customer retention is built by consistently delivering value, creating meaningful and seamless consumer experiences, and building products that customers want to continue using over time. You are passionate about understanding what drives long-term engagement and loyalty, and translating those insights into experiences and product improvements that strengthen the consumer relationship throughout their health journey. 

**Responsibilities:**

Own the End-to-End Consumer Journey

* Own and continuously improve the full D2C customer lifecycle, from purchase and onboarding through engagement, retention, renewal, and advocacy.
* Map the complete customer journey and identify friction points, drop-off moments, and opportunities to improve the experience.
* Develop a best-in-class onboarding experience that helps consumers quickly understand the value of SiPhox and successfully begin their health journey.
* Create thoughtful customer touchpoints throughout the lifecycle to ensure consumers remain engaged and understand the value they are receiving.

Drive Retention and Reduce Churn

* Develop and execute strategies to improve consumer retention and minimize churn.
* Identify the key drivers of customer churn and develop proactive strategies to address them.
* Build customer segmentation and lifecycle strategies based on behavior, engagement, needs, and risk of churn.
* Develop proactive outreach and engagement strategies for customers who may be at risk of disengaging.
* Continuously test and improve retention initiatives, customer communications, and product experiences.
* Establish clear retention and engagement metrics and regularly report insights and opportunities to leadership.

 Be the Voice of the Customer

* Build strong systems for collecting, synthesizing, and acting on customer feedback.
* Develop a deep understanding of consumer needs, motivations, pain points, and expectations.
* Bring customer insights directly to Engineering & Product, Sales & Marketing, and leadership.
* Ensure that recurring customer issues and requests are translated into actionable product and operational improvements.
* Conduct customer interviews, analyze qualitative feedback, and identify emerging trends and opportunities.

 Partner Closely with Product and Sales & Marketing

* Work closely with Product and S&M to improve the consumer product experience.
* Help prioritize product improvements based on customer feedback, friction points, and business impact.
* Contribute to product roadmap discussions and advocate for the consumer perspective.
* Identify opportunities to improve the customer experience through product features, automation, personalization, education, and engagement.
* Partner with Product and S&M to define and improve the key moments that drive customer activation, engagement, and long-term retention.

Build a Scalable Customer Experience Organization

* Design scalable processes for customer onboarding, support, relationship management, and retention.
* Determine where a high-touch, human relationship can add value and where automation can improve the customer experience at scale.
* Develop playbooks and workflows for key customer moments, including onboarding, engagement, customer recovery, and retention.
* Partner with Operations and Customer Support to ensure customer issues are resolved effectively and insights are captured.
* Over time, help build and lead a high-performing consumer experience and customer success organization.

Use Data to Improve the Consumer Experience

* Define and track key customer lifecycle metrics, including activation, engagement, retention, churn, satisfaction, and lifetime value.
* Analyze customer behavior and identify patterns that predict successful long-term engagement or churn.
* Use data and experimentation to prioritize initiatives and measure impact.
* Develop dashboards and reporting that provide visibility into the health of the D2C customer base.

**What Success Looks Like**

In this role, success means creating a consumer experience that makes customers feel supported, engaged, and continuously connected to the value of SiPhox.

Key measures of success may include:

* Improved customer activation and onboarding completion
* Increased consumer engagement
* Reduced customer churn
* Improved subscription renewal and retention
* Increased customer lifetime value
* Improved customer satisfaction and loyalty
* Faster identification and resolution of customer pain points
* A stronger feedback loop between consumers and the Product organization
* A scalable customer experience model that can grow with the business

**What We're Looking For**

* 7+ years of experience in Customer Experience, Customer Success, Product, Consumer Strategy, Growth, or related roles.
* Experience working with a direct-to-consumer, subscription, digital health, healthcare, wellness, or consumer technology business.
* Strong product instincts and experience partnering closely with Engineering & Product, S&M.
* Deep understanding of customer lifecycle management, engagement, retention, and churn reduction.
* Highly analytical, with the ability to use data to identify opportunities and measure impact.
* Exceptional empathy for consumers and a strong ability to understand customer needs.
* Experience conducting customer research and translating customer feedback into actionable insights.
* Strong cross-functional leadership skills and the ability to influence without direct authority.
* Comfortable operating in a fast-paced, high-growth startup environment.
* Entrepreneurial mindset with a willingness to build processes and systems from the ground up.

**The Ideal Candidate**

The ideal candidate is someone who naturally asks:

Where are customers getting stuck?

Why are customers leaving?

What value are our most successful customers receiving that others are not?

How can we make the experience simpler, more personalized, and more valuable?

What should we build next based on what consumers are telling us?

You are equally comfortable talking directly with customers, analyzing retention data, working with a Product team on the roadmap, and designing a strategy to improve the entire consumer experience.

Most importantly, you believe that strong customer retention is earned by continuously delivering value and creating an exceptional experience and product that customers genuinely want to continue using and engaging with over time.

### **Compensation and Benefits**

* Stock options, and meaningful equity in a company solving a problem that matters.
* Luxury gym membership (Lifetime Backbay) Boston, MA, US fulltime yes

### **About Chasi**

Every building, road, warehouse, and farm runs on equipment like tractors, cranes, forklifts, etc. Over 100K dealers and rental companies across North America keep those machines bought, sold, rented, and serviced, but most still operate on phone calls, paper, and decades-old software, with fewer people to do the work every year.

Chasi is building the future of equipment commerce. We help dealers and rental companies sell faster, respond to customers around the clock, and keep machines in the field instead of sitting in a shop or a yard. This is one of the biggest opportunities to bring real-world AI to an industry that software has barely touched. We're based in San Francisco, backed by YCombinator and other top investors, and already working with CAT, John Deere, Bobcat, and other top OEM dealers.

### **About the role**

This is a customer-facing, technical founding role. You own getting Chasi live at dealers, driving real adoption, and proving ROI — then expanding the account.

You're not a ticket-taker and you're not pure sales. You're the person who makes the product work in the wild. As we scale, this seat can grow into broader ownership across strategic product, growth, and partner initiatives — the work that compounds beyond a single account.

### **What You'll Do**

**Near term (deployment + outcomes)**
- Own onboarding end-to-end: kickoff through go-live for dealer and rental accounts
- Deploy Chasi into real workflows (sales, parts, service, rental) and remove what blocks adoption
- Be the technical point of contact — diagnose issues, map processes, escalate cleanly to eng when needed
- Define success with each account (response time, quote speed, conversion, utilization, revenue impact) and run the loop until ROI is obvious
- Drive expansion: more users, locations, use cases, stronger renewals
- Bring customer truth back to product — ranked by impact

**As you grow into the role**
- Shape strategic product direction from what you see in the field
- Own or co-own growth initiatives that turn successful deployments into a repeatable motion
- Help build partner initiatives (OEMs, dealer groups, channel) that scale distribution and deployment
- Build playbooks and eventually help hire/train the next deployment hires

### **Who You Are**

- You've done technical, customer-facing work (implementation, solutions, technical CS, consulting, forward-deployed-adjacent — coding optional, technical judgment required)
- You earn trust with operators who aren't software-native (GMs, sales managers, service leads)
- You're commercially minded: adoption without ROI isn't success; expansion is part of the job
- You want a seat that can expand — product, growth, and partners — not a fixed CSM lane forever
- You move fast, own outcomes, and don't wait for a perfect playbook
- Bonus: equipment, industrial, automotive, logistics, or other field-heavy verticals

### **Other Details**

- In-person, San Francisco
- Reports to CEO
- Base $120,000 – $160,000 + commission + meaningful early-stage equity
- Customer travel and long weeks expected

## Compensation

The base pay range for this role is $120,000 – $160,000 per year, plus commission and equity.

The QA Engineer will be responsible for ensuring the quality of our software products through meticulous manual testing. You will work closely with developers, product managers, and other stakeholders to identify defects, verify functionality, and ensure an exceptional user experience. This role focuses on hands-on testing, test case creation, and detailed reporting to maintain high standards of software quality.

## Responsibilities

* **Test Planning and Design**: Create detailed, comprehensive, and well-structured test plans and test cases based on product requirements and specifications.

* **Regression Testing**: Perform regression testing to ensure new changes do not negatively impact existing functionality.

  * Strong understanding of software testing methodologies, including functional, regression, and exploratory testing.

  * Excellent attention to detail and problem-solving skills.
  * Strong communication skills to articulate defects and collaborate with cross-functional teams.

  * Experience testing web and/or mobile applications.

AiPrise is a YC-backed (S22) global compliance orchestration platform helping fintechs, marketplaces, and payment companies verify and onboard customers worldwide. We integrate with 80+ identity and compliance vendors to deliver a holistic view of risk. We're building AI-powered compliance agents to transform KYB, AML, sanctions screening, and risk scoring, enabling customers to onboard faster, reduce manual reviews, and prevent financial crime.

We operate across 200+ countries.

## **The Role**

This is not a typical engineering role. As a Forward Deployed Engineer, you'll sit at the intersection of engineering, product, and customer success. You'll work directly with AiPrise's largest and most strategic customers to understand their compliance challenges, build custom integrations, and ship solutions that make the platform indispensable.

You won't be waiting for a ticket to land in your queue. You'll be in the room with the customer, scoping the problem, writing the code, and deploying the fix, sometimes in the same day.

This role is ideal for engineers who get energy from solving real problems for real people, and who want their work to have visible, immediate impact.

## **What You'll Do**

**Customer-facing engineering.** Embed with key customers to understand their onboarding, KYB, and compliance workflows. Translate their pain points into technical solutions, whether that's a custom integration, a new API endpoint, or a workflow tweak.

**Build and ship fast.** Design and deploy customer-specific configurations, integrations with third-party compliance and identity vendors, and custom data pipelines. Own the full lifecycle from scoping through production.

**Bridge product and engineering.** Bring customer insights back to the core product team. Identify patterns across customer needs that should become platform features. Help shape the roadmap based on what you're seeing in the field.

**Technical problem-solving under pressure.** Debug production issues in real time. Troubleshoot complex vendor integrations across 80+ providers. Be the person customers trust to get things working.

**Scale what works.** Turn one-off solutions into reusable patterns. Write internal tooling, documentation, and runbooks that make the next deployment faster for everyone.

## **What We're Looking For**

- 3+ years of software engineering experience building and shipping production systems. You've written code that real users depend on.

- Strong backend fundamentals. Proficiency in at least one modern language (Python, Go, Java, Node.js). Experience with REST APIs, microservices, and relational databases (PostgreSQL, MySQL).

- Customer-facing comfort. You can hold your own in a call with a VP of Compliance at a fintech. You listen well, communicate clearly, and know how to translate business language into technical requirements (and vice versa).

- Spanish fluency required. You can read and write in Spanish to support our Spanish-speaking customer base directly.

- Bias toward action. You don't wait for perfect specs. You scope, build, and iterate. You're comfortable with ambiguity and thrive when given ownership.

- Cloud experience. Hands-on with AWS (preferred), GCP, or Azure. Familiar with CI/CD, Docker, and modern deployment practices.

## **Nice to Have**

- Experience in fintech, regtech, payments, or fraud/risk detection

- Familiarity with compliance workflows (KYC/KYB, AML, sanctions screening)

- Experience integrating with third-party APIs at scale

- Frontend skills (React, TypeScript) for building internal tools or customer-facing dashboards

- Background working with ML/AI systems or data-intensive applications

## **Why This Role**

- Your work has direct, measurable impact on customers and revenue. No abstraction layers between you and the outcome.

- You'll learn the compliance and fintech space deeply, working across diverse customer environments.

- You're joining a 36-person, fast-moving team where your code hits production in days, not months.

- Competitive compensation with meaningful equity in a YC-backed company with strong momentum.

- In-person team in San Jose, working alongside the founders and core engineering team.

## **About Bree**

Bree is a consumer finance platform that brings better, faster, and cheaper financial services to over half the Canadian population who live paycheck to paycheck. We operate in a huge, but overlooked market in a country with the least amount of financial technology innovation in the developed world. Our first act is to become the cheapest and best provider of short-term credit to the 20 million people in Canada who live paycheck to paycheck.

More than 800,000 Canadians have already signed up with Bree and we believe we are just scratching the surface. We are in an exciting place where we have product market fit, explosive growth, and a clear path to becoming one of the most important FinTechs in Canada.

You’ll contribute to real modelling and data problems, learn how production ML systems are evaluated and monitored, and use AI tools thoughtfully to move from experimentation to reliable implementation.

This is an **8-month** co-op term.

### **About Corgi**

Corgi is vertically integrating the entire insurance industry. We design, underwrite, price, and issue insurance directly. Insurance is the largest unautomated industry in financial services, and we're rebuilding it from the ground up using AI. We've raised $374M from Kindred, TCV, and others to do so.

Building something great requires working hard. We are in the office 6-7 days a week. We are meritocratic with very high standards. If you don't meet them, you'll get cut. But if you deliver, you have unlimited scope to grow.

We move quickly, care deeply about talent density, and hire people who want to solve difficult problems with unusually high ownership.

We’re hiring hard-working, high-energy early-career sales reps to join our in-person team in Dallas, Chicago, and Atlanta.

This is a ground-floor sales role where you’ll learn outbound, talk to property managers daily, and move fast.

Our AI Agents help compliance teams do more with less, resolving more cases, catching more fraud, and scaling operations without scaling headcount.

We're ~60 people, Series A funded, and obsessed with a single problem: making compliance feel simple for the teams who live in it every day.

Borders shouldn't be blockers. Compliance is hard. AiPrise shouldn't be.

 

 

## The Role

As a Product Designer II at AiPrise, you'll own design for a defined feature area of our compliance platform end to end, turning complicated processes, data, and decisions into clear, intuitive experiences.

Our platform serves compliance analysts reviewing flagged cases, compliance managers configuring the rules that decide what gets flagged, business customers completing verification for the first time, and our own Forward-Deployed Engineering team standing up and supporting customer workflows. Depending on where you're working, you'll design for several of them.

You'll work with product and engineering to take defined problems from discovery through launch. The problem and its owner will be clear; how it gets solved is where you come in. We move fast and share work early, so expect feedback from customers and teammates to shape your designs while they're still taking form.

You'll partner closely with product and engineering, with enough proximity to leadership to see why decisions get made and how your work lands with customers. Our priorities and processes will keep evolving as we grow, so you'll prioritize your own work with limited oversight and change course when new information arrives.

 

 

## What You'll Do

### Design Judgment

- Make design decisions independently within your feature area, applying and extending our design system where it needs to stretch.

- Weigh user needs, design quality, delivery speed, business priorities, and technical constraints, and catch usability problems before they reach engineering.

- Build working domain expertise in the compliance and verification workflows your feature area touches, deep enough to connect your day-to-day design work to roadmap goals and explain how it ladders up to quarterly objectives.

### Execution

- Own medium-complexity projects end to end, from discovery and exploration through final design, implementation, and launch, with minimal oversight.

- Create clear user flows, prototypes, final designs, and documentation, anticipating edge cases and the non-happy paths that make compliance software either trustworthy or infuriating.

### Customer & Data Insights

- Combine customer conversations, usability testing, and product analytics to validate design decisions and identify problems worth solving, rather than only responding to the feedback in front of you.

- Work with internal teams who sit closest to customers to pressure-test what you're seeing in the data.

### Communication & Influence

- Partner closely with product and engineering to clarify the problem, requirements, constraints, and measures of success.

- Explain your design rationale clearly, contribute confidently in product and planning discussions, and keep stakeholders current on progress, risks, and open questions.

- Help newer designers get better, through design reviews, feedback, and pairing on tricky problems.

 

 

## What We're Looking For

- 3+ years as a product designer, with a track record of shipping features and workflows to customers.

- Experience designing complex B2B, enterprise, fintech, compliance, identity, fraud, risk, or other data-heavy products, where the hard part was the information and not the interface.

- A portfolio that shows how you frame problems, use research and data, explore solutions, and make design decisions, not just the final screens.

- Fluency in interaction design, information architecture, visual design, and prototyping, with the attention to edge cases and implementation quality that complex products demand.

- Clear written and verbal communication, and a collaborative approach to working with product managers and engineers.

We are looking for a Security Architect to own the security architecture of our platform end to end, across infrastructure, applications, and APIs, and to be hands-on in making it better. This is a builder’s role, not a paper one. You will work shoulder to shoulder with engineers to find and fix real security issues, set the standards that keep them fixed, and translate a demanding regulatory landscape into practical controls the team can actually ship.

You will also be the technical face of security in the rooms that matter: with auditors, with enterprise customers’ security teams, and with regulators. You will join as an individual contributor with the depth to lead by doing, and as the security team grows you will have the opportunity to build and manage a team of your own.

- Own the security architecture across cloud infrastructure, applications, and APIs, and evolve it as the platform grows into new products and regions.

- Work directly with engineers to identify, prioritize, and remediate security issues in infrastructure, application code, and APIs, reviewing designs, pairing on fixes, and validating that they hold.

- Define and maintain security standards, reference architectures, and hardening baselines, and drive their adoption across engineering.

- Lead and coordinate security testing, including penetration tests, vulnerability management, and remediation tracking, and hold findings to closure within defined timelines.

- Translate industry and regulatory security and privacy requirements into concrete technical and organizational controls, and keep them current as obligations change.

- Own the technical side of audits and assessments, including industry and certification audits (for example SOC 2 and ISO 27001), enterprise-customer security reviews, and regulatory reviews, covering evidence, control mapping, and remediation of findings.

- Represent security in customer-facing conversations, including security questionnaires, due-diligence calls, and trust discussions with prospects, customers, and their auditors.

- Partner with the privacy and data-protection function to ensure controls meet GDPR and other applicable data protection requirements, with particular care for personal and biometric data.

- Contribute to incident readiness and response, including detection, investigation, and post-incident improvement.

- As the team grows, mentor and eventually manage junior security engineers, setting technical direction, reviewing work, and developing the team.

## **What We're Looking For**

- 7 to 9 years of experience in security engineering, security architecture, or a closely related field, with a track record of securing production systems at scale.

- Genuine hands-on technical depth. You can read and reason about application code, cloud infrastructure, and API design, and work with engineers to fix issues rather than only flagging them.

- Strong command of cloud security, including network segmentation, IAM, secrets and key management, and workload and container security, along with infrastructure-as-code.

- Deep application and API security knowledge, including the common vulnerability classes (for example access-control flaws, injection, and SSRF), secure design patterns, authentication and authorization, and secure SDLC practices.

- Solid, current understanding of industry and regulatory security and privacy requirements, such as SOC 2, ISO/IEC 27001, GDPR, and related frameworks, and the judgment to apply them proportionately.

- Demonstrated experience handling audits and assessments of multiple kinds (certification, enterprise-client, and regulatory), including preparing evidence and driving findings to closure.

- Excellent stakeholder and customer-facing communication. You can explain security clearly and credibly to engineers, executives, auditors, and customers alike.

- Sound risk judgment. You can balance security, business needs, and delivery, and make defensible decisions with incomplete information.

## **Nice to Have**

- Experience in fintech, regtech, identity verification, or another regulated, data-sensitive domain.

- Experience handling personal or biometric and identity data and the associated privacy obligations.

- Background in penetration testing, red teaming, or vulnerability research.

- Familiarity with privacy frameworks and regulations beyond GDPR (for example regional data protection laws), and with DevSecOps practices and tooling.

- Relevant certifications (for example CISSP, CCSP, OSCP, or privacy certifications such as CIPP or CIPT) are valued, but hands-on capability matters more.

- Experience mentoring or leading engineers, with an interest in building and managing a team.

## **Growth and Leadership Track**

This role is designed to grow. You will start as a hands-on individual contributor with real ownership of our security architecture. As the security function expands, you will have a clear path into leadership: building, mentoring, and managing a team while continuing to set technical direction.

## **About the interview**

1. Introductory Discussion (Engineering Manager) – 45 mins

3. Security Deep Dive – 60 mins

## About AiPrise

AiPrise is a YC-backed (S22) global compliance orchestration platform helping fintechs, marketplaces, and payment companies verify and onboard customers worldwide. We integrate with 80+ identity and compliance vendors to deliver a holistic view of risk. We're building AI-powered compliance agents to transform KYB, AML, sanctions screening, and risk scoring, enabling customers to onboard faster, reduce manual reviews, and prevent financial crime. 

We operate across 200+ countries.

## The Role

This is not a typical engineering role. As a Forward Deployed Engineer, you'll sit at the intersection of engineering, product, and customer success. You'll work directly with AiPrise's largest and most strategic customers to understand their compliance challenges, build custom integrations, and ship solutions that make the platform indispensable.

You won't be waiting for a ticket to land in your queue. You'll be in the room with the customer, scoping the problem, writing the code, and deploying the fix, sometimes in the same day.

This role is ideal for engineers who get energy from solving real problems for real people, and who want their work to have visible, immediate impact.

## What You'll Do

**Customer-facing engineering.** Embed with key customers to understand their onboarding, KYB, and compliance workflows. Translate their pain points into technical solutions, whether that's a custom integration, a new API endpoint, or a workflow tweak.

**Build and ship fast.** Design and deploy customer-specific configurations, integrations with third-party compliance and identity vendors, and custom data pipelines. Own the full lifecycle from scoping through production.

**Bridge product and engineering.** Bring customer insights back to the core product team. Identify patterns across customer needs that should become platform features. Help shape the roadmap based on what you're seeing in the field.

**Technical problem-solving under pressure.** Debug production issues in real time. Troubleshoot complex vendor integrations across 80+ providers. Be the person customers trust to get things working.

**Scale what works.** Turn one-off solutions into reusable patterns. Write internal tooling, documentation, and runbooks that make the next deployment faster for everyone.

## What We're Looking For

* **3+ years of software engineering experience** building and shipping production systems. You've written code that real users depend on.
* **Strong backend fundamentals.** Proficiency in at least one modern language (Python, Go, Java, Node.js). Experience with REST APIs, microservices, and relational databases (PostgreSQL, MySQL).
* **Customer-facing comfort.** You can hold your own in a call with a VP of Compliance at a fintech. You listen well, communicate clearly, and know how to translate business language into technical requirements (and vice versa).
* **Bias toward action.** You don't wait for perfect specs. You scope, build, and iterate. You're comfortable with ambiguity and thrive when given ownership.

# Head of Customer Engineering

**Location:** San Jose

**Employment Type:** Full time

**Location Type:** On-site

## Why this role exists

AiPrise is building the global compliance operating system for modern fintechs, marketplaces, banks, and platforms. We are trusted by leading financial institutions and process millions of onboarding decisions across KYC, KYB, AML, fraud, and monitoring.

We are past figuring out product market fit. We are now scaling complex, global customer deployments at speed.

Every customer we onboard is a high stakes, high complexity technical lift. Compliance teams are trusting us with their core regulatory workflows, and the integration work, configuration decisions, and workflow design that happen in the first weeks determine whether a customer thrives or churns. Time to first verification is our north star, and customer engineering is where that is won or lost.

We are looking for a Head of Customer Engineering to lead our Forward Deployed Engineering (FDE) team. This person sits at the intersection of the customer and the product team. They are the voice of the customer inside the company, and they make sure every customer is set up for success from day one.

This is a builder, a technical leader, and a customer champion in one role.

## What you will own

### 1. The Forward Deployed Engineering team

- Lead, grow, and level up our team of FDEs deployed across our customer base

- Set the bar for what great forward deployed work looks like: deep product knowledge, strong engineering judgment, and genuine ownership of customer outcomes

- Define how FDEs are staffed against customers by tier, complexity, and region

- Build hiring loops, onboarding programs, and career paths that turn strong engineers into exceptional customer-facing ones

### 2. Customer onboarding and integrations

- Own time to first verification as a primary company metric

- Design and run the end to end technical onboarding journey from contract signed to live in production

- Lead FDEs through integration architecture, workflow configuration, sandbox validation, and go-live for both technical and non technical customers

- Create clean handoff rituals from sales to customer engineering to support

- Ship onboarding and integration playbooks that scale across SMB, mid market, and enterprise

### 3. Voice of the customer

- Be the strongest advocate for the customer inside the company

- Build a structured, high signal feedback loop from the field into product and engineering: what customers are asking for, where they struggle, and what would make them expand

- Translate messy customer signal into crisp product requirements, prioritized and backed by evidence

- Partner with product on roadmap decisions, bringing real deployment data and customer context to every debate

- Close the loop back to customers when their feedback ships

### 4. Customer success through engineering

- Ensure every customer is set up for success: correct integration patterns, sound workflow design, and configurations that will scale with their volume

- Own technical escalations end to end, from triage through resolution and postmortem

- Partner with engineering on customer impacting incidents and drive fixes with urgency

- Use AI aggressively across the team: agents that triage tickets, investigate issues, and accelerate integrations

- Build the self serve layer, documentation, and tooling that lets customers move fast without waiting on us

### 5. Founder level partnership

- Act as a thought partner to the founders on customer strategy, deployment models, and scale

- Join key customer calls, POCs, enterprise escalations, and critical incidents

- Influence tooling, staffing models, and service tier definitions

- Represent customer engineering credibly with customers, partners, and investors

## What success looks like in 12 to 18 months

- Median time to first verification is cut by at least half

- Every strategic customer has a clear technical owner and a documented path to success

- Product and engineering treat customer engineering as their most trusted signal on what to build next

- Customers name their FDE relationship as a reason they stay and expand

- Technical escalations resolve faster quarter over quarter, with fewer repeats

- The team ships with strong ownership and clarity without founder involvement in daily deployments

## Who you are

We are looking for someone who is opinionated, technically sharp, and relentlessly customer driven.

You likely have:

- 10 plus years in solutions engineering, forward deployed engineering, sales engineering, or technical customer-facing leadership

- Experience scaling a customer-facing engineering function at a Series A to Series C B2B SaaS, infrastructure, or fintech company

- A track record building an FDE, solutions, or implementation function from scratch

- Deep comfort with APIs, integrations, and enterprise technical sales cycles. You can read code, debug an integration, and whiteboard an architecture with a customer's engineering team

- Experience translating customer needs into product direction and holding your ground in roadmap debates

- Comfort operating with ambiguity, speed, and high ownership

- A strong bias toward action over decks

Bonus:

- Compliance, KYB, KYC, fraud, payments, or regtech background

- Experience across global customer bases including LATAM, Africa, SEA, and MENA

- You have deployed AI tooling in a customer-facing engineering org and have strong opinions on where it works

- Experience running POCs and technical evaluations against competitors

- Familiarity with tooling such as Pylon, Linear, Intercom, or Zendesk

You are:

- Able to go from messy customer signal to product requirement to shipped outcome

- Comfortable saying no to a customer and explaining why, and equally comfortable pushing product to say yes

- Respected by engineers because you are one

- Energized by hard problems and real world impact

- Excited to build in a fast moving, founder led environment

## Why AiPrise

- Category defining problem in global trust and compliance

- Real scale with millions of checks and global coverage

- AI native from the ground up

- Strong revenue growth and enterprise traction

- Founders who are deeply product and engineering driven

- Massive whitespace ahead

## About AiPrise

AiPrise is a global compliance orchestration platform helping fintechs, marketplaces, and payment companies verify and onboard customers worldwide. We integrate with 80+ identity and compliance vendors to deliver a holistic view of risk. We're now building AI-powered compliance agents to revolutionize KYB, AML, sanctions screening, and risk scoring — enabling our customers to onboard faster, reduce manual reviews, and prevent financial crime.

## About the Role

We are looking for a Security Architect to own the security architecture of our platform end to end, across infrastructure, applications, and APIs, and to be hands-on in making it better. This is a builder’s role, not a paper one. You will work shoulder to shoulder with engineers to find and fix real security issues, set the standards that keep them fixed, and translate a demanding regulatory landscape into practical controls the team can actually ship.

You will also be the technical face of security in the rooms that matter: with auditors, with enterprise customers’ security teams, and with regulators. You will join as an individual contributor with the depth to lead by doing, and as the security team grows you will have the opportunity to build and manage a team of your own.

## What You’ll Do

* Own the security architecture across cloud infrastructure, applications, and APIs, and evolve it as the platform grows into new products and regions.
* Work directly with engineers to identify, prioritize, and remediate security issues in infrastructure, application code, and APIs, reviewing designs, pairing on fixes, and validating that they hold.
* Perform threat modeling and security design reviews for new services and significant changes, and embed security into the development lifecycle (secure coding standards, code review, CI/CD controls, dependency and container security).
* Define and maintain security standards, reference architectures, and hardening baselines, and drive their adoption across engineering.
* Lead and coordinate security testing, including penetration tests, vulnerability management, and remediation tracking, and hold findings to closure within defined timelines.
* Translate industry and regulatory security and privacy requirements into concrete technical and organizational controls, and keep them current as obligations change.
* Own the technical side of audits and assessments, including industry and certification audits (for example SOC 2 and ISO 27001), enterprise-customer security reviews, and regulatory reviews, covering evidence, control mapping, and remediation of findings.
* Represent security in customer-facing conversations, including security questionnaires, due-diligence calls, and trust discussions with prospects, customers, and their auditors.
* Partner with the privacy and data-protection function to ensure controls meet GDPR and other applicable data protection requirements, with particular care for personal and biometric data.
* Contribute to incident readiness and response, including detection, investigation, and post-incident improvement.
* As the team grows, mentor and eventually manage junior security engineers, setting technical direction, reviewing work, and developing the team.

## What We're Looking For

* 7 to 9 years of experience in security engineering, security architecture, or a closely related field, with a track record of securing production systems at scale.
* Genuine hands-on technical depth. You can read and reason about application code, cloud infrastructure, and API design, and work with engineers to fix issues rather than only flagging them.
* Strong command of cloud security, including network segmentation, IAM, secrets and key management, and workload and container security, along with infrastructure-as-code.
* Deep application and API security knowledge, including the common vulnerability classes (for example access-control flaws, injection, and SSRF), secure design patterns, authentication and authorization, and secure SDLC practices.
* Solid, current understanding of industry and regulatory security and privacy requirements, such as SOC 2, ISO/IEC 27001, GDPR, and related frameworks, and the judgment to apply them proportionately.
* Demonstrated experience handling audits and assessments of multiple kinds (certification, enterprise-client, and regulatory), including preparing evidence and driving findings to closure.
* Excellent stakeholder and customer-facing communication. You can explain security clearly and credibly to engineers, executives, auditors, and customers alike.
* Sound risk judgment. You can balance security, business needs, and delivery, and make defensible decisions with incomplete information.

## Nice to Have

* Experience in fintech, regtech, identity verification, or another regulated, data-sensitive domain.
* Experience handling personal or biometric and identity data and the associated privacy obligations.
* Background in penetration testing, red teaming, or vulnerability research.
* Familiarity with privacy frameworks and regulations beyond GDPR (for example regional data protection laws), and with DevSecOps practices and tooling.
* Relevant certifications (for example CISSP, CCSP, OSCP, or privacy certifications such as CIPP or CIPT) are valued, but hands-on capability matters more.
* Experience mentoring or leading engineers, with an interest in building and managing a team.

## **Growth and Leadership Track**

This role is designed to grow. You will start as a hands-on individual contributor with real ownership of our security architecture. As the security function expands, you will have a clear path into leadership: building, mentoring, and managing a team while continuing to set technical direction. # Founding Forward Deployed Engineer

You’re a builder who works at the frontier with our customers. You deploy Nessie into customer environments, build the integrations and workflows they need, and bring what you learn back into the core product. We’re two people with more real customer pull than two people can carry, so you’re the technical and product force that makes deployments real, and you wear the hats a tiny company needs. You make our customer operations and relationships faster across the board.

---

## **What "build" means here**

* You have shipped something real: something with users, or something you use every day because you made it for yourself. You have gone from nothing to working software more than once.
* You’re comfortable across the stack. Our codebase is Swift/SwiftUI (macOS app), Go (backend), and TypeScript (services). You do not need experience in all of these. You need to be the kind of person who picks up what they need.
* You reach for AI tools instinctively (Claude Code, Cursor, Codex) and you are faster because of it. If your first instinct under pressure is to stare at the code instead of handing it to an agent, this is not the right fit.

---

## **What you will work on**

**Core engineering**

* Cross-platform conversation sync across many AI providers, the hardest unsolved capture problem in the space
* Search and retrieval that makes thousands of conversations queryable in milliseconds
* Ontology and knowledge structuring: turning messy conversational material into trustworthy, typed knowledge
* AI governance: team sharing, permissions, and policy. This is what turns Nessie from an individual tool into the context layer for a whole organization.
* Agent-facing APIs (CLI, MCP) that let any AI tool reach accumulated human reasoning
* Self-hosted and on-prem deployments, plus the security and compliance that come with them, as we move into larger and more regulated organizations
* The intelligence layer that sits underneath every AI interaction
* Agent-trace intelligence: extracting the first-class signal that lives only inside AI sessions and agent traces into a queryable layer for observability, eval, and self-improving agent workflows

**Forward deployment**

* Embed with a customer to deploy Nessie into their environment: onboarding, the team-sharing and permissions rollout, integrations, and live troubleshooting, alongside the founders. You shadow first; the founders stay the relationship leads. Increasingly this includes self-hosted or on-prem setups for larger or regulated orgs.
* Own the customer feedback loop operationally: triage, reproduce, drive the fix with us, and make sure nothing slips.
* Build the integrations and glue a specific customer needs, in a way that re-packages into the product.
* Absorb operational work so we can all keep shipping. What you work on in week 1 may differ from week 4.

**A bit of everything**

* We keep this part intentionally broad. On a two-person team, beyond shipping product you'll help with internal ops, owning customer relationships, and the work that does not fit a job title. If you want to only write code and never touch anything else, this is not the role.

---

## **What you will NOT need**

* A specific degree or school
* Prior startup experience
* A perfect resume
* Permission to try things

## **What you will need**

* The instinct to ship before it is perfect
* Extreme autonomy. We are two people. There is no manager. There is no spec. There is a problem and you figure out how to solve it.
* Opinions about products you use. If you have never looked at an app and thought "this is wrong and here is how I would fix it," we are probably not a match.
* Comfort with ambiguity. The product is evolving fast, and what you work on in week 1 may differ from week 4. That should excite you.

---

## **Logistics**

* San Francisco, in person.
* $100K-150K salary, 0.5%-1.0% equity.
* We’re open to sponsoring work authorization (including H-1B) for the right person.

## **How to apply**

Show us something you built. A link to a project, a repo, a product, a tool. If you do not have something to show, build something this week and send it. We care about what you make, not what you say you can make. San Francisco, CA, US fulltime possible

Now we scale and one key lever is the platform. Every new customer brings new data sources, more rows to sync, and more queries to serve. Your job is to make sure ZeitMind can handle onboarding 10 new enterprise customers per week and the hard part isn't the compute. It's capturing each business's context fast enough: connecting messy data systems, making sure the agent's answers are correct, that visualisations hold up, and that the customer is able to get value out of the product quickly. This is as much a product and correctness problem as an infrastructure one, and it hasn't been solved before. Onboarding a customer should be boring. This is the role that lets everything else scale.

## What you will do

* Build the sync layer: millions of rows from ERP, CRM, and homegrown systems, ingested incrementally and reliably, without an engineer babysitting the pipeline
* Cut onboarding time: connecting a new customer's data sources should take hours, not weeks. You abstract sources so our agents work with any of them the same way
* Make the agent fast where it counts: speed comes from tool design that parallelizes, sub-agents, and branching, not tokens per second. You design tools so work can run concurrently and safely
* Route data safely between customer networks and ours: security and reliability are features our customers pay for
* Build the guardrails for correctness: automatic checks and integrated validation tooling so the agent's output can be trusted, and so it flags what a human should verify
* Keep the platform simple: choose boring technology where boring wins, and be able to say why every system we run earns its place

## You will thrive here if you

* have built or scaled data platforms before and think clearly about data processing architectures

We're looking for a design engineer who obsesses over how software looks and feels to join us in San Francisco. You'll own the product surface end-to-end–from concept to pixel-perfect production code–and make Circleback's design go from really good to elite.

## **Why Design at Circleback**

Design is core to Circleback’s strategy. We’re product-led, and one of the hardest problems we have is making something powerful enough for sophisticated teams while still feeling simple and intuitive to anyone who opens it.

You’ll have a huge amount of ownership over what Circleback looks and feels like. One of your first priorities will be establishing and codifying our design system, then carrying it consistently across web, Mac, Windows, iOS, and Android. You’ll work directly with a small engineering team that cares deeply about craft and wants to push the product bar higher.

From there, the problems get much more open-ended. We already have customers with 500+ seats using Circleback to search and reference what’s been said across their company. The next step is helping them make sense of all of that context without having to go looking for it: proactively organizing, synthesizing, and surfacing what matters. There isn’t an established interface for this yet. You’ll help invent it.

Longer term, Circleback is becoming much more than a meeting note-taker. We’re building the operational source of truth for a team: a horizontal product that can understand and represent everything from a candidate or customer to a project or decision across dozens of conversations. That means designing flexible primitives like tables, charts, and workflows, while figuring out how those building blocks should adapt to completely different kinds of work.\
\
You’ll also work on growth and because Circleback grows through the product itself, seemingly small improvements to onboarding, activation, and collaboration can have an outsized impact on the business.

And this role can grow with the company. As we build out the design function, there’s a path to leading it: identifying what we need next, shaping how design operates at Circleback, and eventually building the team around you.

## What you'll do

We're looking for a design engineer who obsesses over how software looks and feels to join us in San Francisco. You'll own the product surface end-to-end–from concept to pixel-perfect production code–and make Circleback's design go from really good to elite.

Most companies split design and engineering into separate roles, separate teams, separate conversations. We don't want that. We want one person who can look at a feature, know how it should work, open Figma, open their editor, and ship it. No handoff. No fidelity gap. What you design is what users get.

Circleback already has a product that customers love. Your job is to take that foundation and push it to the level of the best-designed software in the world. That means:

* Own the design and frontend implementation of features across web (React, Next.js), desktop (Electron, Swift), and mobile (React Native)
* Deeply understand customer problems and find elegant ways to solve them–Circleback deals in dense, conversational information, and making that feel effortless to navigate is a genuinely hard design problem
* Craft interactions, animations, and transitions that make the product feel fast and alive
* Build and evolve our design system–components, patterns, tokens–so quality scales as we ship faster
* Sweat the details other people skip: loading states, empty states, error states, keyboard shortcuts, hover treatments, the feel of a drag interaction
* Iterate quickly on experiments around onboarding, activation, and education
* Work directly with engineers and founders on product direction–you'll shape what we build, not just how it looks
* Prototype new ideas quickly in code, not just mockups–the best way to evaluate an interaction is to use it

## Who you are

You're a designer who codes or an engineer with exceptional taste–either way, you can take an idea from sketch to shipped product without waiting on anyone else. You build things for fun. You've done this before, and you have a portfolio or shipped work that shows it.

You care about craft at a level most people find unreasonable. You'll iterate on an animation curve five times. You'll notice when padding is 3px off. You have strong opinions about typography, color, and spacing–and you can articulate why something feels wrong, not just that it does. You understand that the best product experiences are often invisible.

You're fast and pragmatic. You'd rather ship something great today than something perfect next month. You'd rather write a bit more code yourself than adopt a dependency. You're interested in the challenge of making powerful tools without compromising simplicity–and you can keep a broad set of customer perspectives in mind while doing it.

You're excited about AI as a tool–both in the product you're designing and in your own workflow. You use things like Cursor or Claude Code and have opinions about how AI should show up in product interfaces.

### Intro

Jochen and I have known each other since 2019. We started this company in 2025 in the energy space. Mid-2025 we sold our tech (home energy management systems for households with EVs, solar and heatpumps) to find a new market. During that time we first noticed how many consumers were already asking ChatGPT for advice before putting solar panels onto their roof. And our partners were left wondering why their competitor showed up and they didn’t. Looking deeper at the problem we closed a pilot with one of the largest insurances in the world and 3 months later, we were accepted into YC W26.

Today, the GEO market is moving from tracking AI visibility to operationalizing optimization. Teams no longer just want to know whether they show up in ChatGPT, Gemini, or Perplexity. They are building the workflows to take action every day: define a strategy, create better content, build the right pages, earn the right mentions, and understand what levers actually change how AI systems talk about them.

We believe GEO will be a full marketing discipline. Agents will increasingly shape buying decisions, so companies need to market to humans and agents at the same time. Sitefire is building the analytics and execution layer for that shift:

1. the place marketing teams go to understand their brand's AI visibility, sentiment, and traffic
2. the agents that execute the actions to win more customers.

Under the hood, this means working with large, fast-growing datasets (\~50M+ rows) and turning them into signal for our agents.

### The Role

We are hiring our first engineer in Munich: a Founding Product Engineer who can own full product features end to end. You will work directly with the founders and customers, figure out what to build, ship it, and keep improving it until it creates real customer value.

This is a high-intensity, founder-style role for someone who wants ownership, speed, and direct exposure to customers. It is not a narrow frontend, backend, or platform role.

It is also a chance to help build a truly AI-native company in Munich. We want AI to be part of the operating system of the company: how we build product, review work, improve agents, learn from customers, and create self-improving loops around the business.

### Your First 90 Days

In your first 90 days, you will help turn Sitefire from an analytics product with agents into the platform marketing teams run their GEO agents on.

You will work directly with us and our customers to understand where agents can create real leverage: not just generating drafts, but taking useful actions inside marketing workflows.

You will likely spend your first months on work like:

* Expanding what Sitefire agents can do by adding more external connectors, deeper workflow integrations, and more specialized expert agents.
* Building the quality systems around those agents, including evals, review flows, customer-facing controls, and feedback loops that make the system better over time.
* Joining customer jour fixes and sales calls to learn the market, understand what teams actually need, and see where the product is still too manual.
* Demoing the product and the features you build directly to customers, then using their feedback to improve them quickly.
* Scoping new agentic features with customers so Sitefire integrates more deeply into their marketing stack.
* Shipping end-to-end product work across frontend, backend/data systems, LLM pipelines, and UX.

If timing lines up, you will also fly to San Francisco with us for two weeks this fall to work from the center of the YC ecosystem, meet founders and customers, and sharpen how we build the company.

By the end of your first 90 days, you should have shipped meaningful product improvements, built customer context, and changed what our agents are capable of.

The work spans product thinking, frontend, backend systems, LLM pipelines, data, and customer conversations. You should enjoy that range.

### What We Are Looking For

We are looking for a builder who can own a feature without needing a full team around them.

We are trying to find our sustainable maximum. We work intensely, in person, and with very high standards. At the same time, we care about staying clear-headed, managing stress, and treating each other as humans, not just output machines.

In normal weeks, expect office-first work and a high pace. When someone needs a break, we take that seriously.

Take superconducting qubit devices from post-fab packaging to operational readiness. Own chip mounting and cryogenic assembly including wirebonding, shielding, and thermalization. Design or adapt microwave-compatible printed circuit boards and enclosures for clean signal routing and filtering. Build and maintain dilution refrigerator setups including fridge wiring, line commissioning, and the attenuators, filters, isolators, circulators, switches, and low-noise amplifiers that go with them. Develop robust procedures for cooldowns and thermal cycling to maximize uptime.

### Qubit calibration and characterization

Take devices from cooldown to working qubits. Run core calibrations including resonator and qubit spectroscopy, Rabi, Ramsey, echo, energy relaxation and coherence times, readout optimization, and two-qubit gate calibration. Drive coherence, readout performance, and calibration time in the right direction, and know which one is limiting you.

### Calibration automation

Encode expert tuning into software the platform runs on its own. Turn spectroscopy, gate calibration, and readout optimization into routines that recover without a physicist in the room. Close the loop with the software and machine learning teams.

### System performance and control stack

Keep systems stable and online. Diagnose and mitigate spurs, crosstalk, leakage, two-level system defects, thermal population, and wiring or component failures. Define the monitoring, health checks, and recovery a superconducting system needs to run unattended. Lead setup and scaling of the experimental lab environment, and write or adapt control software for arbitrary waveform generators, microwave sources, direct current sources, digitizers, and field-programmable gate arrays.

* Fix the friction point you found in your first month, and propose the highest leverage things the team can do in superconducting qubits.

* Have at least one calibration improvement in production that has moved a key metric. Coherence, readout fidelity, and time to a calibrated device are examples of what we track.
* Lead superconducting operations at Conductor.
* Drive the control and calibration roadmap, including which systems we bring onto the platform next.

## The team

We are a small, passionate founding team of quantum physicists, hardware engineers, and machine learning experts. Our founders, Brandon and Joel, met each other at Oxford during their PhDs working on AI for quantum computing. There they saw first-hand that calibration and control is a core bottleneck to scaling quantum computers.

This is your opportunity to do the best work of your life as part of that founding team.

Our software automates calibration and operations across qubit platforms, turning raw hardware into a stable, ready-to-run platform accessible through a simple chat interface. ### Overview:

Polymath Robotics is creating software that can safely control all of the world's industrial vehicles, and we're looking for a Sr. Robotics Controls Engineer to join our team. Polymath was founded by Stefan Seltz-Axmacher and Ilia Baranov. Stefan previously founded Starsky Robotics, one of the first companies to run a fully unmanned truck on a public highway. Ilia previously led robotics teams at Amazon, Clearpath Robotics. We started Polymath because every industrial vehicle company was rebuilding the same autonomy stack from scratch, badly, and we figured we could build it once, properly.

Our vehicles are heavy and unforgiving: haul trucks, wheel loaders, excavators, tractors, and port machinery. Making a 40-ton articulated machine track a path smoothly and handle its implements safely is the core of what we do.

### Responsibilities:

* Be a leader on the team, with significant industry experience, to mentor others in controls best practices.
* Design, implement, and tune vehicle controllers across a wide range of industrial platforms: path tracking, speed control, articulated and Ackermann steering, and implement/hydraulic control (booms, buckets, blades).
* Own the vehicle dynamics layer: system identification, actuator characterization, and building control strategies that work across machines with different mass, geometry, and actuation.
* Integrate with drive-by-wire systems over CAN/J1939, working directly with DBW integrators to specify feedback signals, fail-safe behavior, and loss-of-comms handling.
* Contribute to our work in ROS2, filling in the gaps and enhancing our architectural framework where controls meets planning and behavior.
* Design and validate safety-critical behaviors: safe-stop trajectories, protective stop response, and graceful degradation when sensors or actuators misbehave.
* Commission and tune controllers on real vehicles at customer sites, from mines to farms. Expect some travel, and expect to find out whether your PID holds in the field.
* Communicate with prospective clients to align expectations and ensure our control capabilities cover their vehicles and use cases.
* Maintain high ownership of your work, witnessing firsthand the impact of your controllers on customer vehicles performing real tasks.

### Your First 90 Days

* **First 30:** get a vehicle moving. Learn our stack (ROS2, our controls layer, the DBW interfaces), drive our test platforms in sim and in the yard, and read the commissioning logs from past deployments to see where controllers actually break.
* **By 60:** own the controls work stream for an active customer vehicle. Run system identification, tune path tracking and speed control, and defend your decisions in design reviews.
* **By 90:** commissioning support for new vehicles. You'll be validating your controller on the real new machine at full payload, and you'll own the punch list that comes out of it.

### Qualifications:

Expertise in one or more of the following: classical and modern control (PID, MPC, LQR, pure pursuit), vehicle dynamics and system identification, CAN/J1939 and drive-by-wire integration, C++, Python, ROS/ROS2. 6+ years previous experience working on autonomous robots or vehicles, including time spent tuning controllers on physical machines rather than only in simulation. A passion for high ownership of work and a collaborative spirit, with the ability to contribute anywhere on the stack as needed. In a given week, you can jump from system identification on a wheel loader, to chasing a steering fault on the CAN bus, to organizing with the team to efficiently split work and find common features.

Experience with hydraulics, heavy equipment, or functional safety standards (ISO 13849, ISO 3691-4) is a plus.

## About Bree

Bree builds better, faster, cheaper financial services for the half of Canadians living paycheck to paycheck. We were part of Y Combinator (Summer 2021) and raised a $2M seed round shortly after. Team of <20, \~80% engineers, no red tape or politics. We move fast because we have to — and because it's more fun that way.

## Why this role exists

Our engineering team ships. Our growth engine works. What we don't have yet is the connective tissue between vision and execution.

You'll be the operating system between strategy and delivery — working directly with the founders to run the OKR cadence, write the briefings that compress a leadership decision from five days to five minutes, kill the meetings that don't earn their seat, automate the reports nobody should be running by hand, and quietly own the projects no one else has time for.

This is the role for someone who left consulting or banking because they wanted to build — not just write recommendations and hand them off.

## What you'll actually do

**Run the rhythm.** Own OKR planning, weekly business reviews, and the quarterly cadence. Every person on the team should know what they're working on, why it matters, and how it ladders up to the number that matters most. If they don't, that's on you.

**Be the bridge.** Engineering, growth, and operations don't always speak the same language. You translate. You unblock dependencies before they become blockers. You hold the line on priorities when "urgent" crowds out "important."

**Fix the systems, not the symptoms.** When something breaks twice, you redesign it. When a recurring report takes four hours every Monday, you make it run itself. We don't want a process bureaucrat, we want someone who builds machines that don't need them.

**Be genuinely AI-native.** We're an AI-native team and lean heavily on LLMs and agents: internally, in tooling, and to replace manual workflows wherever they slow us down. The right person already uses these tools as leverage in their daily work.

**Write the one-pager.** Distill messy, multi-variable problems into something an exec can act on in three minutes. The "so what" matters more than the deck.

**Own the work without a home.** Special projects, vendor negotiations, ad-hoc analysis, the post-mortem nobody wants to write — the in-between projects land with you. You take them from zero to one, then build the system that runs without you. Occasionally, you'll PM a feature when the moment calls for it.

**Live in the data.** SQL is table stakes. You write your own queries. You reach for the data before the opinion.

## Who we're looking for

* **4+ years relevant experience**: consulting, investment banking, high-growth startup BizOps/Strategy, or strategic finance.
* **First-principles problem solver**: You start with _why_ - why the process exists, what the true constraints are, what's the simplest thing that could work - before jumping to _how_. You build before you ask permission.
* **Obsessed with data.** You don't make claims you can't quantify. You're suspicious of any decision that can be measured but isn't.
* **Extreme attention to detail and highly organized.** You re-prioritize constantly and context-switch without dropping things. Nothing slips through your system, because you've actually built one.
* **Technically literate.** You don't ship production code, but you read SQL fluently, hold your own with engineers on a tradeoff conversation, and understand technical constraints.

## Why us

We started CoLoop in 2020 while still at university. We survived multiple cofounder breakups and all sorts of other near-death experiences. Despite that we built our first product to $1M ARR, and then killed it after realising the opportunity was too small and we didn't have real PMF. We spent six months pivoting, and through that process came to understand just how important customer research is to finding a winning strategy. So we built a product to make it faster, cheaper, and better.

We don't tell you this because we think suffering is something to aspire to. We tell you because if you're evaluating where to work next, you should know who you'd be working with. We are not going to sell early, get comfortable, or lose interest. This is everything to us.

We also take seriously that you're trusting us with your time. Three people who've worked at CoLoop have gone on to become YC founders. When you're here, we'll share everything we know and everything we learn along the way. All we ask is total commitment.

---

## About the role

You'll spend most of your time understanding customers, thinking about what to build, and shipping. Talk to customers directly, sit with the team members who interact with them daily, watch the recordings (in CoLoop). AI handles a lot of the raw building now, so the bottleneck is taste, context, judgement, and polishing.

At CoLoop, engineers own the full cycle. There are no product managers. You gather context from customers and teammates, decide what to build, build it, launch it, measure the impact, and iterate. We track individual attribution in PostHog.

The structure is flat. Influence is earned through skill and context. We'd rather you make a wrong call than wait to be told what to do.

We run 5-6 week company-wide sprints with a decentralised approach and minimal meetings. We're in our Oxford Circus office as often as possible (2 days min per week).

Your work will span three main areas:

Making the product feel exceptional. CoLoop is used daily by researchers at some of the best companies in the world. You'll own UI/UX improvements that make the product faster, clearer, and more delightful to use.

Growing the product. We're building a product-led motion. You'll design and ship in-app growth experiments, lead magnets, onboarding flows, and activation loops that move conversion and retention numbers.

Building for our customers. Some of the world's best research teams rely on CoLoop. You'll build bespoke features and integrations that make them wildly successful, and turn those into product capabilities that benefit everyone.

---

## What we're looking for

* You care deeply about the end user's experience. You notice when padding is off, when a loading state is missing, when a flow has one too many steps.
* You're commercially minded. You think about what moves revenue, not just what's interesting to build.
* You have an artisan's mindset toward your craft. You can explain what makes Linear great, both as a company and product. You know that AI makes good engineers faster but doesn't replace taste and craftsmanship.
* You know when to cut corners and when to be rigorous. Move fast at the edges, build carefully at the core.
* You want to get on call to fix a gnarly bug even though somebody else caused it.
* You recognise you have blind spots and want other people to point them out, and will happily return the favour.

### Must-haves

* 2+ years full-stack experience building web applications.
* Strong React and TypeScript.
* Comfortable using AI coding tools (e.g. Claude Code) as part of your daily workflow.
* Fluent English.

### Nice-to-haves

* You've worked on PLG or growth engineering.
* You've been a founding engineer at a high-growth company, or founded one yourself.
* You've contracted or consulted on projects for enterprise-scale clients. People who've operated end-to-end for paying customers tend to think commercially, and that matters here.

### No AI experience needed

Our product is AI-native, and you'll be working alongside engineers who build AI systems every day. The day-to-day for this role is product work, not AI work. But you'll absorb a lot by proximity, there's scope to take on AI projects over time, and if you're great at it, to move into that kind of work entirely.

---

## What you get

* You work directly with the founders and founding team on a daily basis.
* You join a tight-knit team of engineers: physics PhD, hackathon winner, and more.
* You work alongside engineers building cutting-edge generative AI, including our multi-agent system for qual content analysis. You won't be siloed from that work.
* You become part of a community of top technologists in London. We regularly host dinners, hackathons, and [CoLoop CoWorking](https://events.coloop.ai/) from our office most Saturdays.

---

## How to apply

* 1-line introduction about yourself.
* 1-2 lines on what you've built and what you took away from it.
* A URL to a live project, repository, or open source contribution you made.
* 1-2 lines on your interest in CoLoop and how you'd contribute.

---

## Interview process (\~1–2 weeks)

1. Screening interview (30 min)
2. Technical interview (60 min)
3. In-person contract
   1. 1 week trial (preferred)
   2. 1 day trial (if unable to do 1 week)
4. Decision

---

If you're excited about this role but don't meet every requirement, we'd still love to hear from you. If you'd like to meet the team, we host [CoLoop CoWorking](https://events.coloop.ai/) from our office most Saturdays! ### What will you be working on?

As our 3rd sales hire you will be working on prospecting, qualifying and nurturing target leads whilst honing the required skills to move ultimately into running discovery calls, closing and negotiation ever large contracts as an AE.

You’ll work closely with our CEO Jack, Senior Account Executive Kieran and first SDR Reece on:

### **About Bunkerhill**

Bunkerhill partners with leading health systems to design and deploy AI-enhanced clinical workflows that are used in real clinical operations. We work directly with clinicians, operations leaders, and IT teams to turn messy clinical reality into scalable, high-impact AI workflows.

## **About the Role**

We’re hiring an **S-tier Technical Implementation Program Manager** to own **end-to-end customer delivery** of the **Bunkerhill Carebricks** AI platform across multiple health systems. Carebricks sits on top of the EHR (primarily Epic Systems) and also integrates with ancillary systems (PACS, web portals, etc.).\
**2026 reality:** each customer will have **\~10+ use cases**, many are net-new and variable.

## **What You’ll Do**

This person will independently own the customer lifecycle across multiple use cases:

* **Discovery:** clarify workflow + data sources + triggers + required writebacks; define architecture & scope.
* **Ingestion enablement:** guide customer teams to stand up cohort feeds / triggers (SQL extracts, HL7, Bulk FHIR, etc.).
* **Data integrity:** validate end-to-end flow and reconcile against Epic/ancillary systems.
* **Runtime enablement:** install/configure Epic on FHIR app (OAuth2 background user, security points, etc.); guide SMART on FHIR where relevant.
* **Writebacks:** implement best writeback channel per use case (FHIR create APIs, HL7 Z-segments, portal APIs, SMART workflows).
* **Execution:** build and enforce plan, manage risks/dependencies, drive internal engineering + customer IT to hit deadlines through go-live + hypercare.

## **Required skills**

**A) EHR + interoperability integration depth**

* Proven delivery experience integrating with EHRs (ideally Epic Systems) and/or major health-system IT environments.
* Hands-on fluency across **HL7 v2**, **FHIR R4**, **OAuth2 / app registration**, and interface troubleshooting.

**B) Data ingestion + validation**

* Experience with cohort feeds / triggers via **SQL extracts** (e.g. Epic Clarity), HL7 feeds, and/or Bulk FHIR.
* Can run (or direct) **data integrity validation**: sampling, reconciliation, edge cases, monitoring.

**C) Writeback architecture**

* Track record writing results back into EHRs or clinical systems via:
  * FHIR create APIs (e.g., docs/observations/notes patterns)
  * HL7 customization (Z-segments)
  * External portal APIs / webhooks
  * SMART-based workflow patterns (nice-to-have but strong signal)

**D) Implementation ownership**

* Has owned implementations end-to-end: discovery → build → go-live → hypercare (post-live), with measurable outcomes.

### **Why Bunkerhill**

* Real impact at leading health systems. Our Carebricks platform is live at UTMB Health, Cleveland Clinic, Mayo Clinic, and dozens of other hospitals across the U.S., powering workflows like incidental findings follow-up, prior authorization, referral routing, and more.
* Award-winning AI implementation. Bunkerhill was recently named “Best in AI Implementation” in **_Inc.’s 2025 Best in Business Awards_ for the way Carebricks lets clinical and operational teams build and deploy AI agents that actually run in day-to-day workflows.[ Business Wire](https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20251202974653/en/Bunkerhill-Health-Named-Best-in-AI-Implementation-in-Inc.s-2025-Best-in-Business-Awards?utm_source=chatgpt.com)**
* Backed by top-tier investors. We’re backed by Sequoia Capital, Felicis, Optum Ventures, SciFi VC, SV Angel, and others, with a raised $30M Series A led by Sequoia and Felicis.
* Recognized as one of AI’s “killer apps.” Sequoia highlighted Bunkerhill as part of the rising cohort of “AI’s Killer Apps” in its AI Ascent keynote, alongside companies like LangChain and OpenEvidence. [**LinkedIn**](https://www.linkedin.com/posts/bunkerhill-health_excited-to-see-sequoia-capital-recognize-activity-7331331055146127360-62HO?utm_source=chatgpt.com)
* Regulatory and clinical credibility, not just demos. Our platform incorporates multiple FDA-cleared algorithms, including models for cardiovascular findings such as aortic valve and mitral annular calcification, now deployed as part of Carebricks in real clinical workflows.
* You’re joining at an inflection point: revenue has leapt from early pilot scale to multi-million-dollar ARR in the last year, as health systems standardize critical workflows on Bunkerhill
* A chance to help define the category. Bunkerhill’s mission is to close the gap between the potential of AI in healthcare and its reality in clinical practice. As one of the first Forward Deployed Product Leads, you’ll help define how health systems design, ship, and scale AI-enhanced workflows—not just at one hospital, but across a growing network of top institutions.
